Description:
Two cylinders of the SAME radius whose axes cross at a right angle - the textbook case of an INNER
TANGENTIAL CONTACT with crossing intersection curves.
cylZ is a cylinder of radius 10 about the z axis, cylY the same cylinder about the y axis. Because the
radii are equal, the intersection of the two infinite mantles degenerates into TWO ELLIPSES, lying in
the planes z = y and z = -y, and those two ellipses CROSS at the two points
  (10, 0, 0) and (-10, 0, 0)
At each of them both surfaces have the same tangent plane (x = +-10) and the intersection curve has a
NODE - two branches crossing at one point - which is the degeneracy this case is about.

The axes are chosen so that the nodes land on the WORST POSSIBLE spot of the topology: a cylinder about
the z axis through the origin is split into its two half mantles exactly in the xz plane, so its seam
edges are the lines x = +-10, y = 0. The two nodes sit exactly ON those seams - tangential contact,
crossing of the two intersection branches and face boundary all in the same point.
See EqualCylindersObliqueNode for the same contact placed in the interior of the faces.

The two cylinders are deliberately of DIFFERENT and ASYMMETRIC length, z from -20 to 30 and y from -20
to 25. That has no effect on the contact - the axes still cross at the origin and the intersection body
stays inside |y|, |z| <= 10 - but it makes the two halves each difference falls into differ in volume.
With symmetric cylinders those halves are congruent, and then the canonical order of the parts of a
multi solid result is not determined and the recorded extents flip from run to run.
Expected:
V(cylZ) = pi*100*50 = 15707.9632679490, area 2*pi*10*50 + 2*pi*100 = 3769.9111843078,
edgeLength 4*pi*10 + 2*50 = 225.6637061436, extent -10,-10,-20 .. 10,10,30.
V(cylY) = pi*100*45 = 14137.1669411541, area 3455.7519189488, edgeLength 215.6637061436,
extent -10,-20,-10 .. 10,25,10.

The intersection is the STEINMETZ SOLID of two equal cylinders, whose volume and area are known exactly:
  volume  16*r^3/3     = 5333.3333333333
  area    16*r^2       = 1600.0000000000  (no cap is reached, the body stays inside |y|,|z| <= 10)
  extent  -10,-10,-10 .. 10,10,10
It is a single solid bounded by four cylindrical faces meeting at the two nodes, with no planar face.

From that everything else follows exactly:
  union        15707.9632679490 + 14137.1669411541 - 5333.3333333333 = 24511.7968757697
  cylZ - cylY  15707.9632679490 - 5333.3333333333 = 10374.6299346156
  cylY - cylZ  14137.1669411541 - 5333.3333333333 =  8803.8336078207

The SHAPE of the differences is the interesting part. In the plane z = 0 the cross section of cylZ is
the full disc of radius 10 and cylY removes all of it, so cylZ minus cylY falls apart into a lower and
an upper half connected ONLY through the two node points (10,0,0) and (-10,0,0):
  pi*100*20 - 5333.3333333333/2 = 3616.5186405129   and   pi*100*30 - 2666.6666666667 = 6758.1112941027
and likewise cylY minus cylZ, split in the plane y = 0 into
  3616.5186405129   and   pi*100*25 - 2666.6666666667 = 5187.3149673078
What must NOT happen is that a half is dropped or that two halves are welded into a manifold body.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. All four operations return and every value meets its calculated expectation to
about 1e-6. Stable over 4 runs.

HISTORY, because the case earned it. As written, two of the four operations did not return at all: the
union (call id 4) and cylY minus cylZ (call id 6) both hit the assertion "loops.Count should never be
0" in BooleanOperation.Result. The defect was not symmetric - cylZ minus cylY returned and was exactly
right - so it depended on the order in which the faces of the two operands were visited, not on the
geometry. The intersection was right from the start as well, which means the two crossing ellipses and
their two nodes were always computed properly; what failed was what got built from them.
In the running application the same two calls FROZE the process: there the assertion is a modal dialog
raised on the UI thread inside BooleanOperation.Result, so the message loop stopped and the MCP server
answered nothing more - no CPU load, no error, no dialog window to be found. That is how the case was
found in the first place. The harness suppresses the dialog and turns the assertion into a failed call,
which is why the case could live in the suite while the defect was open.

FIXED by the additional plane test in CylindricalSurface (Precision.IsPointOnPlane next to the radius
test when a tangential touch point of a cylinder and an ellipse is accepted): a point at the right
distance from the ellipse centre is only a touch point if it also lies in the plane of the ellipse.
With that, the union comes out as one solid of 24511.7664512 against the exact 24511.7968757697 and
cylY minus cylZ as the two expected parts. Nothing else in the case moved - crossInter, crossZminusY
and both operands match their earlier records to the last recorded digit, so the fix added the missing
results without disturbing the ones that already worked.

RE-RECORDED 2026-08-28 after the second fix of the same day. No value moved - volume, area and extent
of every object are the same to the last recorded digit, and both differences and the union still meet
their calculated expectations. What changed is the PARTITION of two objects: crossInter is now cut into
5 faces instead of 4 (7 edges, 4 vertices, edgeLength 172.749 instead of 152.697) and crossZminusY#0
into 5 instead of 4. The added seam edge is 20.05 long, the length of a seam of the z cylinder over the
height of the Steinmetz body. That is a partition that is less tidy than the earlier one but not wrong:
euler stays 2, the bodies stay closed and consistent, and the geometry is untouched.
